chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Ibn al-Qaddah, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The sneezing is the ratification of truthfulness of a person’s words'.
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of sneezing in Islamic tradition regarding truthfulness?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi links the physical act of sneezing to the validation of speech, reflecting the pre-Islamic and early Islamic cultural belief that sneezing was a sign of divine approval or truthfulness. In Shia scholarly tradition, this is often interpreted not merely as superstition but as a natural sign (ayah) encouraging gratitude and social etiquette, where the sneezer responds with praise to Allah. It underscores the importance of recognizing subtle signs in daily life as confirmations of one's words or actions.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ja’far Bin Muhammad Al Ashary, from Ibn Al Qaddah, from Ibn Abu Umeyr,
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The sneezing is the ratification of truthfulness of a person’s words’.
en.sarwar: 26. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Ash’ari from ibn al-Qaddah from ibn abu ‘Umayr from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: ‘‘The Messenger of Allah has said, ‘
Sneezing is verification of the truthfulness of a person’s words.’”
